title: Greece
subtitle: November 2026
arc: A week in Greece told as a climb from looking up to looking out: grey Athens lanes beneath the Acropolis, the silence of Meteora's rock towers, finally standing on the Acropolis, then a Fiat 500 across Santorini that ends in late golden light over the sea.

acts.name: Cold open
acts.purpose: Flash-forward to the most striking image: the traveller above Oia's rooftops and the sea. Introduces who we follow and what the trip is building toward; the title card follows.

acts.name: Below the Rock
acts.purpose: Athens, 9 Nov, overcast: wandering the lanes on foot and seeing the Acropolis only from below. Anticipation.

acts.name: Stone Towers
acts.purpose: Meteora, 10 Nov: the tone shifts from city lanes to scale and silence. The landscape awe beat.

acts.name: Up Top
acts.purpose: Back in Athens, 12 Nov, now in sunshine: moving through the city, then standing on the Acropolis he looked up at on day one. The payoff.

acts.name: The Island
acts.purpose: Santorini by Fiat 500: road, sea, lighthouse, small discoveries. Lightness and momentum.

acts.name: Last Light
acts.purpose: Golden hour on a Santorini terrace: a human moment, then a quiet look out to sea. Reflection and farewell.

music_note: One instrumental track, building and releasing at act breaks only (never mid-scene). Cold open: a single sustained, airy pad or a solo piano phrase, about 70 bpm, fading under the title. Below the Rock: low, sparse acoustic (guitar or piano), unhurried, about 80 bpm, overcast and curious. Stone Towers: a slow swell (strings or pad) with no beat, so the scale lands in near-silence. Up Top: light percussion enters, mid energy, about 95 bpm, warmer and brighter for the sunny Athens day. The Island: highest energy, a bright and loose rhythm (acoustic guitar, hand percussion) at about 105-110 bpm for the road-trip feel. Last Light: drops back to the opening piano or pad motif, slow, warm, resolving on the ending card and fading to black. Keep it organic, with no EDM drops or trailer hits; it should feel like a real person's holiday film.
